source_text: Quamvis tu, quod monuit Apostolus, ne in morbo desiderii suum vas quisque possideat, non de coniugio, sed de fornicatione accipiendum putaveris;
pass_a_gloss: Although you (Julian), what the Apostle warned, that no one should possess his own vessel in the disease of desire, thought it should be understood not of marriage but of fornication; (Augustine addressing Julian, reporting his reading.)

lemmas.gloss: sickness/disease of desire (Vulgate 1 Thess 4:5 'in passione desiderii'; here Augustine's wording)

pass_b_english: Augustine reports, speaking to Julian: “You thought that the Apostle's warning, that no one should possess his vessel in the sickness of desire (1 Thessalonians 4:4-5), is to be taken not of marriage but of fornication.”

choices.why: Julian distinguishes nuptiae from concupiscentia; do not flatten to 'lust' as a nature-sin substance.
Paul in Julian's citations; keep Apostle not 'Paul' unless Paulus is written.

choices.choice: 2026-11-11 (claude-sumfix-b): the old English was a summary and added a claim the Latin does not make: 'and denied that one's vessel meant one's wife'. In the Latin that is Augustine's counterfactual ('potuisti ... et non improbe negare ...': you could have ... and could fairly have denied ...), not a report of what Julian said. Now a translation of the one clause that reports Julian's reading (Quamvis tu ... putaveris), with Augustine named as the speaker.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded. Julian is not first-English.

bible_refs.note: Linked from Julian's wording or a clear allusion in the excerpt.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Contra Iulianum / Against Julian), including authorities Julian quoted; Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded. This row is Augustine's report; Pass A glosses only the Julian words recoverable here.
